summary.text: A 40-year-old man presented with severe recurrent seborrheic dermatitis during his teenage years. He had previously received topical corticosteroids, topical calcineurin inhibitors, oral antihistamines and anti-inflammatory moisturizers for a period of 10 years with only partial response and recurrence, and occasionally short-course oral prednisolone for flare-ups. A flare-up was present before treatment.

For alleviation of symptoms, 20 mg of lyophilized rose stem cell-derived exosomes was applied to the entire face by electroporation. Redness, scaling and itching improved significantly within 1 day after the initial treatment, with improvement shown at Day 2, and a post-procedural Exobalm moisturizer regimen was prescribed to prevent flare-ups: twice daily for 21 days, nightly for 1 month, then twice weekly for an additional month.

During the six-month follow-up the patient required no additional treatments, with sustained improvement at Month 6 after treatment. A flare-up was shown after 6 months; the authors attributed the flare-up to lack of sleep and PM2.5 exposure, and it presented with a longer symptom-free remission and less severity than the previous flare-up.
